title: Phenolic Compounds of Grapes and Wines: Key Compounds and Implications in Sensory Perception
content:
# Phenolic Compounds of Grapes and Wines: Key Compounds and Implications in Sensory Perception

 Phenolic compounds are a wide family of thousands of natural bioactives well-known for their overwhelming demonstrated health benefits. Particularly in wines, polyphenols and quality are closely interconnected. Indeed, these compounds possess a critical role due to their contribution to organoleptic wine quality as color, astringency, and bitterness. The profile or the composition of certain polyphenols has been even proposed as an analytical tool for authenticity certification. In this sense, although important progress has been achieved, the understanding of the relationship between the quality of a particular wine and its phenolic composition remains one of the major challenges in enology research. But why? If there is an adjective to define wine, it is “complex.” This final complexity of a wine begins with the enormous polyphenolic variability that may be present in grapes influenced by ripening, genetic, or environmental factors, among others. Winemaking process (alcoholic and malolactic fermentation) and wine aging with or without wood contact produce endless reactions giving rise to complex transformations (copigmentation, cycloaddition, polymerization, and oxidation) of polyphenols. This chapter gathers the most relevant information about the composition, variations, and transformations of phenolic compounds from grape to wine including their influence on sensory properties.

title: Rice-Based Fermentation in Brewing: Insights from Sake Production
content:
# Rice-Based Fermentation in Brewing: Insights from Sake Production

 Rice remains underutilized in brewing despite its long history in fermented beverages. Sake is produced through multiple parallel fermentation, in which enzymatic saccharification of rice starch and fermentation occur simultaneously. This process relies on koji (mainly Aspergillus oryzae) to supply amylolytic and proteolytic enzymes. Traditional sake production involves time-intensive steps and controlled environments for koji propagation, which may limit accessibility for brewers who are more familiar with conventional beer production. Recent studies have explored the use of exogenous enzyme systems in the production of rice-based fermented beverages, demonstrating that starch hydrolysis and fermentation can be achieved without reliance on koji. By applying controlled gelatinization and enzymatic hydrolysis steps, fermentable substrates can be generated using defined enzyme preparations. These findings suggest that sake production can be adapted using a western brewing framework. The ability to carry out starch conversion and fermentation more quickly using standard brewing equipment presents a practical pathway for brewers to work with rice beyond its conventional role as an adjunct. This creates opportunities for the development of sake-like beverages and other rice-based products while lowering technical barriers associated with traditional sake brewing. 

学术来源：Technical Quarterly，DOI 10.66969/tq-63-nablab-0107-7。
